clue.text: Doubled extremes of temperature that hurt dog

indicators.note: doubled says the piece built from the next words is written out twice in a row

parts.note: the two extremes of temperature are cold and hot, abbreviated C and H
ow is the cry of someone who has just been hurt

explanation.surface: Something about a dog that suffered from very hot and very cold weather, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold and hot are the extremes, giving C and H; add OW and then write the whole thing again.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Chest pain? Try disease container

parts.note: a judge tries a case, which is to say hears it
TB is short for tuberculosis
an urn is a vessel for holding ashes or tea

explanation.surface: A patient with chest pain is told to try treatment for a disease kept in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is in its courtroom sense: to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion felt as a burning ache behind the breastbone is commonly felt as pain in the chest.

clue.text: English town where one ignites hostilities geck ties?

parts.note: war is open hostilities between nations
a candle's wick is the thing that takes the flame and burns

explanation.surface: An English town where someone starts a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is written in answer order: the hostilities come first, then the thing that is lit. The trailing 'geck ties?' is garbled print and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwick is the county town of Warwickshire in the English Midlands, famous for its castle.

clue.text: Scorer awards fifty in throng

indicators.note: in says the letter for fifty sits inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: a host is a large crowd, a throng
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A composer hands out fifty prizes among a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' is one who writes a musical score, not a goal-getter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst, who wrote The Planets, was a composer, so he scored music.

clue.text: Join drops of moisture up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: dew is the drops of moisture that form overnight

explanation.surface: Instruction to join drops of moisture upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, which unites two people, so it means join.

clue.text: Vegetable about ready once tender elsewhere

indicators.note: about says the vegetable goes around the word for ready

parts.note: a pea is a small green vegetable
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A vegetable nearly ready once it has become tender somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is legal tender, money: the peseta was Spain's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency, and the peseta was formerly the currency of Spain, a foreign country.

clue.text: Ceramic no replica, faked

indicators.note: faked suggests the letters of no replica have been falsified into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: This ceramic is not a copy, yet it has been faked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faked' rearranges NOREPLICA.
explanation.definitionFit: China, the fine translucent material, is a kind of ceramic.

clue.text: Bear with sore head, male, hurt endlessly

indicators.note: head of sore means only its first letter is used

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for hurt is dropped

parts.note: to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A bear with a sore head, a male one, keeps hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb, to put up with, not the animal; ACHE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, just as one may bear it.

clue.text: Crime on newsagent's stand?

explanation.surface: A crime committed at the newsagent's.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE FT, the Financial Times, a paper a newsagent displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a crime; the second reading is the Financial Times newspaper.

clue.text: Just one going in a long way

indicators.note: going in says the letter for one enters the phrase meaning a long way

parts.note: far means a long way off
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Just one person going a long way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and just both describe treatment that is impartial and right.

clue.text: German outfit came in first, putting her nose out of joint

parts.note: a winner who came in first led the field

indicators.note: a nose put out of joint is dislocated, so the letters of her nose are disordered

explanation.surface: A rival came first, so her nose was put out of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of joint' rearranges HERNOSE into ERHOSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather shorts with braces are the traditional dress of Bavaria in Germany.

clue.text: Dance brews into intimate performance, virtually describing this?

definitions.text: Dance brews into intimate performance, virtually describing this?

indicators.note: into says the dance and the brews go inside the trimmed word
virtually means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sex is intimate activity between partners
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic
teas are brews of tea

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of dance would put drinks into an intimate act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims the last letter off the intimate act, leaving SE, which 'into' wraps round the dance and the brews; the closing 'describing this?' makes the whole clue a picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic undressing act is an intimate performance that is also danced.

clue.text: Chamber of gold, extremely large

parts.note: auric is the adjective for gold, from Latin aurum

indicators.note: extremely means take the first and last letters of large

explanation.surface: A room made of gold and extremely large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' is the heart's, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An auricle is an atrium, one of the upper chambers of the heart.

clue.text: Book these for variety show

explanation.surface: Advice to engage performers for a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the Acts of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament; the other is the turns on a variety bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts is a New Testament book, and a variety show is made up of performers' turns.

clue.text: Dud Kent, surf dude

indicators.note: dud means useless or broken, so the letters of Kent and surf are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A useless Kent surfer called a dude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dud' rearranges KENTSURF.
explanation.definitionFit: A funky, hip person is a cool type, a dude in slang.

clue.text: Cutting right into fish, six-footer

indicators.note: into says the letter for right goes inside the fish

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
an ant is an insect, which has six legs

explanation.surface: Cutting a fish open on the right for a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' looks like a tall man; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A trenchant remark is sharp and incisive, so cutting in its figurative sense.

clue.text: A mountain range in India holds son in awe

indicators.note: holds says the range contains the letter for son

parts.note: the Ghats are mountain ranges along India's coasts

explanation.surface: An Indian mountain range keeps a son in awe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aghast is filled with horrified amazement, struck with awe.

clue.text: Unexpected tidings firstly carried by TOTAL bird

indicators.note: carried by says the first letter goes inside the bird

parts.note: the starling is a common songbird

indicators.note: firstly means just the first letter of tidings

explanation.surface: Surprising news carried first by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the first letter of 'tidings', goes into STARLING. The word 'TOTAL' in the held text is a printing garble and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising, coming as a shock that was not expected.

clue.text: Some sleeping partners dribble

parts.note: in bridge South and North are partners, S and N
to ooze is to dribble slowly

explanation.surface: Some sleeping partners are dribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeping partners' are not business partners: 'Some sleeping' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooze is a short nap, so a bit of sleep.

clue.text: Experienced person sorted out accoy accommodation for inexperienced one

indicators.note: accommodation for says the first piece houses the next one
sorted out means put into order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An old hand sorted out a place to stay for a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SORTED into ODSTER, which holds L. The word 'accoy' in the held text is a printing garble.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an older person, one with long experience of life.

clue.text: Cold pub given a counter that's vermilion

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an inn is a pub
a bar is the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A cold pub with a counter painted bright red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is mercury ore, the source of the red pigment vermilion, and names that colour.

clue.text: Demand wizard cages knight with suspicious attitude

parts.note: to ask is to request or demand

indicators.note: cages says the wizard surrounds the knight

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a wizard
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a wizard lock up a knight, eyeing them suspiciously.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking askance is looking sideways with doubt or mistrust.

clue.text: One might have an eye on second dessert

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, dessert

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a second helping of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eye' is a potato's bud, not someone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is slang for a potato, and potatoes have eyes from which shoots grow.

clue.text: Up mountain, two sharp bends and a square

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
the letter Z is drawn with two sharp bends

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain road with two hairpin bends to reach a square.
explanation.walkthrough: Z is the shape of the road sign warning of a double bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: One's tight casket made to seal lot

indicators.note: to seal says the rearranged casket closes around the word for lot
made means fashioned, so the letters of casket are reshaped

parts.note: a heap means a lot, a great amount

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person has a casket made to seal up a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges CASKET into CSKATE, which holds HEAP. 'tight' means stingy, not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a miser, a person who is tight with money.

clue.text: Hard surface given delicate touch I love

parts.note: a pat is a light, gentle touch
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Something hard gets a gentle touch; I love it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved area beside a house, a hard outdoor surface.

clue.text: Given expression of nonchalance, it hit back in self-defence

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: tra-la is a carefree sing-song exclamation
to ram is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Acting casually, someone hits back in self-defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRALA + IT + RAM to read as one backwards run.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo and karate are fighting systems often learnt for self-defence.

clue.text: Fool of a girl appearing topless

indicators.note: topless means with its top removed, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A foolish girl appears topless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Arrest slimy character, no saint

indicators.note: no says the letter for saint is not there

parts.note: a snail leaves a slimy trail

explanation.surface: Arresting a slimy character who is no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slimy character' looks like a criminal but is a garden mollusc.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informal for catching and arresting them.

clue.text: Bird not quite birdie? Nonsense!

parts.note: in golf a birdie is one under par, so par falls just short of it
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A golfer misses a birdie and someone calls it nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdie' is a golf score, not a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured talking bird.

clue.text: Put on clothes one time long ago

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, so the word for put on dresses the word one

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on

explanation.surface: Getting dressed once took a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, not garments; 'Put on' is to stage a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period when tools were made of stone.
